authorship: Editorial supplement; separate from original identification key

structures.name: Skull bone

facts.question: Structure
facts.answer: Skull vault formed mainly by frontal, parietal and occipital bones, with squamous temporal contributions.

facts.question: Function
facts.answer: Protects the brain; cranial sutures join its bones.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Cerebral cortex

facts.question: Structure
facts.answer: Outer grey-matter layer of the cerebral hemispheres, folded into gyri and sulci.

facts.question: Function
facts.answer: Processes sensation, controls voluntary movement and supports language, memory and cognition.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Cerebral vessels (middle cerebral artery and vein branches)

facts.question: Supply
facts.answer: MCA branches supply much of the lateral cerebral cortex.

facts.question: Drainage
facts.answer: Superficial cerebral veins carry cortical blood to dural venous sinuses; arterial supply and venous drainage are distinct.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Leptomeninges

facts.question: Structure
facts.answer: Arachnoid mater and pia mater together.

facts.question: Relations
facts.answer: The CSF-filled subarachnoid space lies between them; pia follows the brain surface into sulci.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Subarachnoid space

facts.question: Location
facts.answer: Between arachnoid mater and pia mater.

facts.question: Contents
facts.answer: CSF, cerebral blood vessels and arachnoid trabeculae.

facts.question: Clinical relevance
facts.answer: Rupture of a cerebral vessel can cause subarachnoid haemorrhage.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Occipital vessels and greater occipital nerve

facts.question: Supply
facts.answer: Occipital artery: branch of the external carotid artery supplying the posterior scalp.

facts.question: Sensory functions
facts.answer: Greater occipital nerve: medial branch of the C2 dorsal ramus supplying much of the posterior scalp.

facts.question: Drainage
facts.answer: Occipital veins drain the posterior scalp and communicate with deep cervical and suboccipital veins.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Anterior cerebral artery

facts.question: Origin
facts.answer: Terminal branch of the internal carotid artery.

facts.question: Supply
facts.answer: Mainly medial frontal and parietal cortex, including the leg area of motor and sensory cortex.

facts.question: Lesion
facts.answer: Typical cortical infarction causes contralateral leg weakness and sensory loss, greater than arm involvement.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Corpus callosum and head of caudate nucleus

facts.question: Function
facts.answer: Corpus callosum: connects the cerebral hemispheres. Caudate head: participates in basal ganglia motor and cognitive circuits.

facts.question: Relations
facts.answer: The caudate head bulges into the anterior horn of the lateral ventricle; the corpus callosum lies above the ventricle.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Anterior horn of lateral ventricle

facts.question: Location
facts.answer: Frontal lobe; medial wall is the septum pellucidum and much of the floor is the caudate head.

facts.question: Contents
facts.answer: CSF; the anterior horn has no choroid plexus.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Lateral ventricle and choroid plexus

facts.question: Function
facts.answer: Choroid plexus produces CSF within the ventricular system.

facts.question: Drainage
facts.answer: Lateral ventricle → interventricular foramen (Monro) → third ventricle.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Posterior horn of lateral ventricle

facts.question: Location
facts.answer: Extends posteriorly into the occipital lobe.

facts.question: Contents
facts.answer: CSF; the posterior horn has no choroid plexus.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Inferior sagittal sinus

facts.question: Location
facts.answer: Free inferior border of the falx cerebri.

facts.question: Drainage
facts.answer: Joins the great cerebral vein to form the straight sinus.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Branch of middle meningeal artery

facts.question: Supply
facts.answer: Supplies cranial dura; parent artery arises from the maxillary artery and enters through foramen spinosum.

facts.question: Clinical relevance
facts.answer: Traumatic rupture can cause an extradural (epidural) haematoma.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Septum pellucidum and columns of fornix

facts.question: Relations
facts.answer: Septum pellucidum separates the anterior lateral ventricles, between corpus callosum and fornix.

facts.question: Function
facts.answer: Fornix columns carry hippocampal output; postcommissural fibres reach the mammillary bodies in memory circuits.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Lateral ventricle and temporalis muscle

facts.question: Function
facts.answer: Lateral ventricle: contains CSF. Temporalis: elevates the mandible; posterior fibres retract it.

facts.question: Innervation
facts.answer: Temporalis is supplied by deep temporal nerves from the mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve (V3).

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Internal capsule

facts.question: Structure
facts.answer: Projection fibres between cortex and subcortical structures; lies between caudate/thalamus medially and lentiform nucleus laterally.

facts.question: Contents
facts.answer: Genu: mainly corticobulbar fibres. Posterior limb: corticospinal and ascending somatosensory fibres.

facts.question: Lesion
facts.answer: Small posterior-limb infarcts can cause dense contralateral weakness.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Insula

facts.question: Location
facts.answer: Cortex deep within the lateral sulcus, covered by frontal, parietal and temporal opercula.

facts.question: Function
facts.answer: Processes taste and internal bodily sensations, with roles in autonomic and emotional integration.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Putamen

facts.question: Structure
facts.answer: Part of the striatum with the caudate; forms the lentiform nucleus with globus pallidus.

facts.question: Function
facts.answer: Participates in basal ganglia circuits that select and regulate movement.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Globus pallidus

facts.question: Location
facts.answer: Medial to putamen; together they form the lentiform nucleus.

facts.question: Function
facts.answer: Internal segment is a major inhibitory basal ganglia output to the thalamus; external segment participates in the indirect pathway.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: External capsule

facts.question: Location
facts.answer: Thin white-matter layer between putamen medially and claustrum laterally.

facts.question: Relations
facts.answer: From putamen outward: external capsule → claustrum → extreme capsule → insular cortex.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Claustrum

facts.question: Location
facts.answer: Thin grey-matter sheet between the external and extreme capsules, deep to the insula.

facts.question: Function
facts.answer: Widely connected with cortex; its precise function remains uncertain.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Posterior crus of fornix and choroid plexus

facts.question: Function
facts.answer: Fornix crus: carries hippocampal output toward the fornix body. Choroid plexus: produces CSF.

facts.question: Relations
facts.answer: The paired crura continue from the hippocampal fimbriae and converge to form the body of the fornix.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Head of caudate nucleus

facts.question: Location
facts.answer: Bulges into the anterior horn of the lateral ventricle.

facts.question: Function
facts.answer: Part of the striatum, involved in motor, cognitive and behavioural circuits.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Tail of caudate nucleus

facts.question: Location
facts.answer: Curves into the temporal lobe along the roof of the inferior horn of the lateral ventricle, approaching the amygdala.

facts.question: Function
facts.answer: Part of the caudate component of the striatum; participates in basal ganglia circuits.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Optic radiation

facts.question: Course
facts.answer: From lateral geniculate nucleus to primary visual cortex around the calcarine sulcus.

facts.question: Lesion
facts.answer: Temporal fibres (Meyer's loop): contralateral superior quadrantanopia. Parietal fibres: contralateral inferior quadrantanopia.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Column of fornix

facts.question: Course
facts.answer: Descends from the fornix body; postcommissural fibres pass toward the mammillary body.

facts.question: Function
facts.answer: Carries hippocampal output in memory circuits; damage can impair memory.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Straight sinus

facts.question: Location
facts.answer: Junction of falx cerebri and tentorium cerebelli.

facts.question: Drainage
facts.answer: Receives inferior sagittal sinus and great cerebral vein; drains toward the confluence of sinuses.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Orbit

facts.question: Contents
facts.answer: Eyeball, extraocular muscles, optic nerve, vessels, nerves, orbital fat and lacrimal gland.

facts.question: Structure
facts.answer: Seven bones: frontal, sphenoid, zygomatic, maxilla, palatine, lacrimal and ethmoid.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Middle cerebral artery

facts.question: Origin
facts.answer: Terminal branch of the internal carotid artery; runs in the lateral sulcus.

facts.question: Supply
facts.answer: Much of the lateral hemisphere; lenticulostriate branches supply deep structures including parts of the basal ganglia and internal capsule.

facts.question: Lesion
facts.answer: Contralateral face/arm weakness and sensory loss; dominant hemisphere involvement may cause aphasia, non-dominant involvement neglect.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Amygdala

facts.question: Location
facts.answer: Anteromedial temporal lobe, deep to the uncus and near the anterior end of the hippocampus.

facts.question: Function
facts.answer: Assigns emotional significance to stimuli, particularly fear; contributes to emotional learning and memory.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Red nucleus

facts.question: Location
facts.answer: Midbrain tegmentum, at the level of the superior colliculus.

facts.question: Function
facts.answer: Motor coordination; receives cerebellar input and gives rise to the rubrospinal tract.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Cerebral peduncle and substantia nigra

facts.question: Contents
facts.answer: Crus cerebri: descending corticospinal, corticobulbar and corticopontine fibres. Substantia nigra lies immediately dorsal to it.

facts.question: Function
facts.answer: Substantia nigra pars compacta supplies dopamine to the striatum; degeneration is central to Parkinson's disease.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Midbrain tegmentum

facts.question: Location
facts.answer: Between the substantia nigra and the region of the cerebral aqueduct.

facts.question: Contents
facts.answer: Red nucleus, reticular formation, cranial nerve nuclei and ascending tracts; supports motor, sensory and arousal functions.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Vermis of cerebellum

facts.question: Location
facts.answer: Midline cerebellar region joining the hemispheres.

facts.question: Function
facts.answer: Coordinates axial movement and posture; lesions typically cause truncal and gait ataxia.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Eyeball and sclera

facts.question: Function
facts.answer: Eyeball: forms images and converts light into neural signals. Sclera: tough fibrous coat supporting globe shape and extraocular muscle attachment.

facts.question: Relations
facts.answer: Sclera is continuous with the cornea anteriorly and the optic nerve's dural sheath posteriorly.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Pituitary gland and cavernous sinus

facts.question: Relations
facts.answer: Pituitary lies in the sella turcica; cavernous sinuses lie laterally and the optic chiasm is superior.

facts.question: Contents
facts.answer: Within cavernous sinus: internal carotid artery and CN VI. In lateral wall: CN III, IV, V1 and V2.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Cerebral aqueduct and tentorium cerebelli

facts.question: Function
facts.answer: Cerebral aqueduct: carries CSF from third to fourth ventricle. Tentorium: dural fold separating occipital lobes from cerebellum.

facts.question: Clinical relevance
facts.answer: Aqueduct obstruction causes non-communicating hydrocephalus; the midbrain passes through the tentorial notch.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Ethmoidal air cells

facts.question: Location
facts.answer: Air-filled spaces in the ethmoid between nasal cavity and medial orbital wall.

facts.question: Drainage
facts.answer: Anterior/middle cells drain to the middle meatus; posterior cells to the superior meatus.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Cerebellar hemisphere

facts.question: Function
facts.answer: Coordinates limb movements; lateral regions contribute to motor planning.

facts.question: Lesion
facts.answer: Typically ipsilateral limb ataxia, dysmetria and intention tremor.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Nasal cavity

facts.question: Function
facts.answer: Filters, warms and humidifies inspired air; olfactory mucosa supports smell.

facts.question: Innervation
facts.answer: Olfaction: CN I. General sensation: mainly trigeminal divisions V1 and V2.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Ocular muscles

facts.question: Innervation
facts.answer: Lateral rectus: CN VI. Superior oblique: CN IV. Remaining extraocular muscles: CN III (LR6, SO4, rest III).

facts.question: Actions
facts.answer: Lateral rectus abducts; medial rectus adducts. Recti and obliques together control elevation, depression and torsion.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Sphenoid sinus and internal carotid artery

facts.question: Relations
facts.answer: Sphenoid sinus lies below the sella; the cavernous internal carotid artery lies close to its lateral wall.

facts.question: Clinical relevance
facts.answer: The sinus provides a transsphenoidal route to the pituitary; carotid proximity creates a risk of major haemorrhage.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Auricle (external ear)

facts.question: Structure
facts.answer: Elastic cartilage covered by skin; the lobule contains no cartilage.

facts.question: Function
facts.answer: Collects sound and directs it into the external acoustic meatus; helps sound localisation.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Cerebellar arteries

facts.question: Origin
facts.answer: SCA and AICA arise from the basilar artery; PICA usually arises from the vertebral artery.

facts.question: Supply
facts.answer: SCA: superior cerebellum. AICA: anteroinferior cerebellum. PICA: posteroinferior cerebellum; territories vary.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Floor of orbit

facts.question: Structure
facts.answer: Mainly maxilla, with zygomatic and a small palatine contribution; lies above the maxillary sinus.

facts.question: Clinical relevance
facts.answer: Blowout fracture may trap orbital tissue/inferior rectus, causing diplopia; infraorbital nerve injury can numb the cheek and upper lip.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Optic canal

facts.question: Location
facts.answer: In the sphenoid at the orbital apex.

facts.question: Contents
facts.answer: Optic nerve (CN II) and ophthalmic artery, with accompanying sympathetic fibres.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Malleus and incus

facts.question: Function
facts.answer: Transmit vibration from tympanic membrane through the ossicular chain to the stapes and oval window.

facts.question: Relations
facts.answer: Malleus handle attaches to tympanic membrane; malleus articulates with incus, and incus with stapes.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Vestibulocochlear and facial nerves

facts.question: Course
facts.answer: CN VII and VIII enter the internal acoustic meatus; CN VII continues in the facial canal and exits at the stylomastoid foramen.

facts.question: Function
facts.answer: CN VIII: hearing and balance. CN VII: facial expression, anterior two-thirds tongue taste, and parasympathetic supply to lacrimal/submandibular/sublingual glands.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Middle ear

facts.question: Contents
facts.answer: Air-filled tympanic cavity containing malleus, incus, stapes, tensor tympani and stapedius.

facts.question: Connections
facts.answer: Pharyngotympanic tube connects to nasopharynx; posteriorly communicates with mastoid antrum and air cells.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Mastoid air cells

facts.question: Location
facts.answer: Air-filled spaces in mastoid temporal bone, communicating with middle ear through the mastoid antrum.

facts.question: Clinical relevance
facts.answer: Middle-ear infection can spread here, causing mastoiditis.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Fourth ventricle and dentate nucleus

facts.question: Location
facts.answer: Fourth ventricle: between pons/upper medulla and cerebellum. Dentate: deep nucleus within each cerebellar hemisphere.

facts.question: Function
facts.answer: Fourth ventricle conducts CSF to subarachnoid space via median and lateral apertures; dentate contributes to planning and coordination of movement.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Coronoid process of mandible

facts.question: Location
facts.answer: Anterior superior projection of the mandibular ramus.

facts.question: Attachments
facts.answer: Insertion of temporalis muscle; involved in elevation of the mandible.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Medial pterygoid muscle

facts.question: Origin
facts.answer: Deep head: medial surface of lateral pterygoid plate. Superficial head: maxillary tuberosity and adjacent palatine bone.

facts.question: Insertion
facts.answer: Medial surface of mandibular angle and lower ramus.

facts.question: Actions
facts.answer: Elevates and assists protrusion of the mandible; unilateral contraction moves it toward the opposite side.

facts.question: Innervation
facts.answer: Nerve to medial pterygoid from mandibular division of trigeminal nerve (V3).

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Lateral pterygoid muscle

facts.question: Origin
facts.answer: Superior head: infratemporal surface of greater sphenoid wing. Inferior head: lateral surface of lateral pterygoid plate.

facts.question: Insertion
facts.answer: Pterygoid fovea on mandibular neck; superior fibres also attach to TMJ capsule/disc.

facts.question: Actions
facts.answer: Protrudes and assists depression of the mandible; unilateral contraction moves it toward the opposite side.

facts.question: Innervation
facts.answer: Nerve to lateral pterygoid from mandibular division of trigeminal nerve (V3).

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Articular disc of temporomandibular joint

facts.question: Structure
facts.answer: Fibrocartilaginous disc dividing the TMJ into upper and lower synovial compartments.

facts.question: Function
facts.answer: Lower compartment mainly permits rotation; upper mainly permits translation during opening/protrusion.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Head of mandible

facts.question: Articulations
facts.answer: Articulates with the temporal mandibular fossa/articular eminence through the TMJ disc.

facts.question: Function
facts.answer: Condyle participates in rotation and translation during jaw movement.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Vermis of cerebellum and dentate nucleus

facts.question: Function
facts.answer: Vermis: axial coordination and posture. Dentate nucleus: major output of lateral cerebellar hemisphere, supporting motor planning.

facts.question: Relations
facts.answer: Vermis is midline; dentate nuclei lie laterally within cerebellar white matter.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Bony nasal septum

facts.question: Structure
facts.answer: Mainly perpendicular plate of ethmoid superiorly and vomer posteroinferiorly; supported by maxillary and palatine crests.

facts.question: Function
facts.answer: Separates the nasal cavities; septal cartilage completes the anterior septum.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Neck of mandible

facts.question: Location
facts.answer: Narrow segment below the mandibular head.

facts.question: Attachments
facts.answer: Pterygoid fovea on its anterior surface receives lateral pterygoid insertion.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Sigmoid sinus and internal jugular vein junction

facts.question: Location
facts.answer: At the jugular foramen, where sigmoid sinus continues as internal jugular vein.

facts.question: Drainage
facts.answer: Carries intracranial venous blood from transverse/sigmoid sinuses into the neck.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Basilar part of occipital bone

facts.question: Location
facts.answer: Anterior to foramen magnum; joins the sphenoid to form part of the clivus.

facts.question: Relations
facts.answer: Clivus slopes behind the sella and lies anterior to the brainstem.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Superior bulb of internal jugular vein

facts.question: Location
facts.answer: Dilated upper internal jugular vein in the jugular fossa, immediately below the jugular foramen.

facts.question: Clinical relevance
facts.answer: A high or dehiscent jugular bulb may lie close to the middle ear and cause pulsatile tinnitus.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.

structures.name: Squamous part of occipital bone

facts.question: Location
facts.answer: Broad posterior part of occipital bone, behind foramen magnum.

facts.question: Attachments
facts.answer: External occipital protuberance and nuchal lines provide ligament and muscle attachments.

structures.authorship: Editorial supplement, created 2026-10-07; not transcribed from the supplied model key.
